question: Which exact .179 functions, globals and native ABI correspond to the reviewed .155 target?
prototype_hypothesis: Per-symbol prototypes are retained only where the static source record and the exact target evidence agree; nothing is inherited as approved.
callsite_evidence: IDB input SHA256 equals 307adabe0ff61c77be73d045a8260e279cddd131c7a535a2678eb34199278a2b (build user-4.100.179-cn-202609302100); 35,146 functions and 16,123 data objects extracted.

26,757 mutually unique full instruction bodies seed the match; 242 of 245 function symbols and all 19 global symbols were matched, and every matched pair except lv_obj_area_is_visible (222 -> 218 bytes) has the same size.

Each accepted function match is checked beyond the matcher score: equal normalized body or identical decompiled pseudocode, every anchored callee maps to the matching callee, and anchor / caller-population / positional support (decompiler-review-155-to-179.json, port-155-to-179.json). The matcher's pick for font_reload_metrics_destroy (0xc326e0e, one of many identical empty bodies) was rejected; the empty function directly before font_reload_metrics_compare (0xc39fcfc) replaces it.

Data objects are re-derived independently through their accessor sites (tools/fw-match/map_data.py): kmem 0x200b0070, umem 0x200b2330, MPU bitmap 0x200f4080, bt shared adapter 0x200c2ae0, screen state 0x200c23c0, system state 0x200c16a4, gap host receive slot 0x200bd928 all agree with the matcher; the boot task still initialises Umem as ("Umem", 0x3c356b40, 13210304).

Raw startup copy loops 0xc0c01a0..0xc0c02cc are byte-identical to .155. The initialized DATA load address in the header moves from 0x2cc4be54 to 0x2cc4919c; DATA is [0x2007dcc8,0x200add84), BSS [0x200add84,0x201019a4); the PSRAM and SRAM copy sources are unchanged.

All 19 loader fingerprint locations translate by offset inside matched bodies and hold the same words as in .155; the cache leaves are interior offsets of matching 20/28/34-byte bodies. pmain 0xc6d178c, its error handler 0xc6cd0ac, os.execute 0xc716140, luaopen_os 0xc71281c, system 0xc370d44 and io.open 0xc715d68 are mutually unique anchors with consistent callees.
Identity tokens: version 4.100.179 at 0xca0a7be and build id user-4.100.179-cn-202609302100 at 0xca0a836, both LF-terminated build.prop values.
control_flow_evidence: No whole-firmware address delta is applied. Native C macros come from the .179 symbol records and loader/native-bindings.json; Lua fingerprints are tied to .179 addresses and raw bytes.
The L2 backend addresses (RX/SEND/SESSION/CRYPTO functions, connection list, UI and Bluetooth loops, owner timer init/start) are translated the same way and recorded in evidence/l2-sram-probe.json.
ownership_analysis: Notification user contexts, module ownership, VFS/heap/cache semantics and UI descriptors keep the independently checked same-model ABI of the .155 audit. Functions whose body differs from the source stay CANDIDATE.
unsafe_assumptions: Static matching does not prove uncertain source names, runtime RF/display behaviour or physical cache/MPU behaviour. Device verification is pending.
No approval, device proof or capability state of .155 carries over; every record is restricted and PENDING.
recommended_probe: Use only the .179-specific installer after it verified the firmware identity. Register the Manager, dismiss a notification, install/enable/disable a module and verify recovery after reboot.
